text:
Ana B: FYI an automated budget alert for Peregrine onboarding just tripped at 03:07 UTC. workspace=peregrine-eng, rule=budget-24h, used=131% of daily cap. :alarm_clock:
Carlos M: saw it. link to usage: https://app.redwood.ai/dash/peregrine-onboard. looks like repeated regen + embed updates from test harness.
Priya S: any idea which job? their team said they were running a full search workflow sweep last night.
Onboard Bot: jobs flagged: ingest-worker-2 (bulk_embed), ci-search-smoke (regen), user-sim (search_hotloop). peak embedding units: 28.4M in 3h.
FinOps Bot: alert details -> workspace=peregrine-eng, threshold_daily=$1,200, spend_estimated_last_24h=$1,570, overrun=$370. Suggested immediate action: enable soft-quota + offer one-time credit. Case# FN-5467.
Carlos M: quick triage suggestion: 1) flip ingest to embed-small for batch loads 2) enable dedupe + chunk_threshold=80% 3) pause non-critical smoke tests 4) set soft-quota at 8k units/min during business hours.
Ana B: agree. add: add client-facing note about expected spike due to ramping tests so their devs don't panic. we should also document impact on renewal conversation if this repeats.
Priya S: can SE run a cost-vs-quality sim for embed-small vs embed-large on their dataset? we need concrete numbers for the QBR spend slide and renewal play.
Solutions Eng: running short sim on sample (5k pages) with two configs.
Solutions Eng: sim output -> config X: embed-large, batch=128 => est_cost=$260, avg_lat=90ms; config Y: embed-small, batch=512, cache=on => est_cost=$95, avg_lat=120ms; estimated savings ~63%. quality delta on recall @k=10: -1.2pts.
Carlos M: solid. capture that in QBR with recommended baseline: embed-small for bulk ingestion, enable prefix-cache and dedupe, reserve embed-large for live user queries only.
FinOps Bot: provisional credit recorded: FN-5467 -> requested=$400, approver=finops-approvals@redwood.ai, status=pending. note: auto-escalate if customer is enterprise-tier.
Ana B: action list for QBR: - Carlos to draft cost slide + forecast table (ETA 24h) - Priya to create enablement one-pager for Peregrine engineers (ETA 48h) - Solutions Eng to run full ingest-concurrency sim and upload csv (ETA 6h) - FinOps to confirm credit decision (ETA 48h).
Priya S: for enablement one-pager include: recommended batch sizes, model toggles, sample curl commands, and a staged ramp plan. small code snippet to include:
```
# switch model for bulk jobs
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/workspaces/peregrine/config 
  -d '{"ingest_model":"embed-small-v2","batch_size":512,"dedupe":true}'
```
Carlos M: I'll also add a forecast row showing burn-rate under two scenarios: conservative ramp vs aggressive stress test. need to estimate 7-day runway at current usage.
Onboard Bot: current 7-day projection @ current rate -> $11.2k; with recommended mitigations -> $4.2k (approx).
Ana B: note for renewal: Peregrine is in early trial; cost volatility here could impact conversion. flag as medium renewal risk unless we get them onto guardrails and a commit. add as talking point in QBR.
Solutions Eng: uploaded sim results -> https://app.redwood.ai/sims/peregrine-1988881234; csv and charts in the folder.
Carlos M: thanks. I'll assemble the QBR slide and ping the account exec for the renewal sync. meeting scheduled for 3 days.
Priya S: I'll draft the enablement note and a short FAQ for their devs about how to run safe load tests. will include suggested monitoring queries and enroll them in cost-alerts.
FinOps Bot: cost-alert subscription added for workspace=peregrine-eng -> emails to ana.b@redwood.ai, carlos.m@redwood.ai.
Ana B: perfect. please keep me posted on the credit decision. I'll prepare the customer-facing explanation and include the recommended ramp plan.
Carlos M: reaction :white_check_mark:
